notes:
PASS on the fake backend only; the evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. This package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run ros-wave-c-130); driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null. No hardware was attached, and no ROS graph, rosbridge connection, Webots process or upstream simulator was run. The clone at 1c45e4bdefb30b8ebbe8e1c4af9b59e22cb0c17f was read only and its git status is clean.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD'S MOCK PREFERENCE: the card prefers upstream-sim, but Webots R2021a, ROS 1 Noetic and webots_ros are not installed where the gate runs, so this package uses a ROS-free canned fake (F0) and makes no upstream-simulator claim. The card's family RosDriver and its decision are kept. The card has no entry_symbols and this is a C++ ROS package, so there is no Python native class and no native.py.

SCOPE: a configuration-only ROS 1 RosDriver over rosbridge, mode simulated, risk R0, device_kind world.sim. The primary interface is the Webots controller service robot/robot/time_step (type webots_ros/set_int). Webots::Init creates the relative service client and sets the request from TIME_STEP (include/webots_ros.h:59-61), the demo constant is 32 (src/demo_2dnav_move.cpp:15), the set_int response is one bool success (srv/set_int.srv:3), and Webots::ChecktimeStep treats a failed call or failed success field as failure (include/webots_ros.h:128-132). One step action sends the fixed value 32; it returns only the acknowledged success and no observation, tick or state hash, which is why cap.world.step.v1 is not used. The observation is /robot/gps/values (geometry_msgs/PointStamped): the gmapping broadcaster enables gps and subscribes to gps/values (src/robot_broadcaster_gmapping.cpp:123-126), includes PointStamped (src/robot_broadcaster_gmapping.cpp:10-11), and its callback reads point.x and point.z (src/robot_broadcaster_gmapping.cpp:85-89). The service and topic names are relative in the clone; the driver records the exact upstream tokens as source_name and configures the resolved root endpoints /robot/robot/time_step and /robot/gps/values. A deployment that namespaces the controller or broadcaster differently must expose those resolved names or change the driver deliberately.

STOP: the e-stop and safe-state path sends robot/robot/time_step with value 0, the request Webots::Quit sends before shutting the ROS node down (include/webots_ros.h:135-141). The same input-free request is declared as the safe_state=True stop action and as safety_bindings.estop; the runtime latches in software before calling it. The clone contains only the client side of that service, not the webots_ros implementation, so the receipt proves only that the controller accepted the 0 request. It does not prove that the controller loop, the world, another ROS client or the Webots GUI stopped, and it is not a physical e-stop. The stop action reports acknowledged (the service success) and does not claim quiescence; the deployment must verify the server-side effect. No physical e-stop exists and no hardware-safety claim is made.

FAKE AND FIDELITY: the fake is a package-local subclass of the SDK's RecordingRosTransport. It answers only call_service on /robot/robot/time_step and subscribe on /robot/gps/values. Engine canned:ROS-free rosbridge fake (no physics), fidelity_level F0, determinism none, timestep_ms 0, realtime_factor 0, reset none, snapshot_restore false. It runs no Webots physics, controller loop, sensors or wall-clock pacing; its step counter, stopped flag, GPS point and frame id are placeholders (# placeholder in fake.py) and are not facts, limits or a replay of captured traffic.

NOT COVERED: the laser scan (robot/Sick_LMS_291/laser_scan/layer0) and its point/range image services, cameras and images, the wheel set_velocity/set_position services, /cmd_vel, /vel, robot/odom, TF, keyboard, joystick, move_base/AMCL/cartographer/gmapping and the rest of the navigation stack. The package does not start Webots, build the catkin workspace, call the gps/inertial_unit/lidar enable services, or validate ROS parameters, QoS, authentication, remapping or reconnection. A live deployment still needs the operator's catkin build, Webots R2021a, ROS 1 Noetic, the webots_ros controller and a rosbridge endpoint; the fake-only pass does not prove runtime construction.

LIMITS AND WARNINGS: no action has a numeric input and the clone states no numeric bound for the time_step value or the GPS sample, so no Limit and no site-limits.example.json are declared. The last gate run passed G1-G7 and G9 and warned only G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because there is no actuating capability with a numeric limit for SAFE-014 to probe; every other CL3 test passed. There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. The source facts cite package.xml:16 for the TODO licence tag (card NOASSERTION), README.md:3 for the Webots R2021a/Ubuntu 20.04 environment, and the pinned controller, world and launch lines for the rest.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') and adds eight repository cases: the fixed step request and its type/args, the 0-value stop request with the acknowledged receipt and fake state, the GPS subscribe sample, a failed service, an application rejection, a missing GPS sample, the e-stop latch with the safe-state action still available, and the shared source-backed service. test_driver also runs inside G9 and passes within the 180 s bound. No network, pip install, upstream import or upstream execution was used; no human review, hardware review or hardware run is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the time_step service and GPS endpoints and types, all 17 facts and the stop. The e-stop and safe-state action were the 0-value robot/robot/time_step request that Webots::Quit sends, unchecked, just before ros::shutdown() and exit(0) (include/webots_ros.h:135-141); the service implementation (the webots_ros ros controller) is not in the clone, the demo controller keeps requesting 32 ms steps in its own loop (src/demo_2dnav_move.cpp:104-107), Webots runs in realtime mode (launch/webots.launch:12-16) and the wheel velocities set from /cmd_vel persist, so nothing shows a stop, yet the SDK reported the e-stop completed. Reviewer removed the estop binding and safe_state=True (the request stays an ordinary action, renamed send_zero_time_step), rewrote safe_state, the docstring and the stop gap, corrected the Quit and licence facts, added three facts (realtime launch, the cmd_vel callback, move_base) and two gaps, dropped the claimed unit '1' from the GPS coordinates (driver.py), added the ROS 1 Header.seq to the fake (fake.py), changed the e-stop cases to expect SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with no request sent (test_driver.py), updated facts.md and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails only G6.ESTOP_FAILED, with the G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warning (stable digest sha256:402e83349ac7e1abde87e9e3f53914eb9e45b7ce813da70ee1eeb746c34a2e63); the ten package cases pass; the author's pass status and stop notes are superseded. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Webots R2021a world with a differential-drive robot that move_base or the keyboard and joystick nodes drive through demo_2dnav_move; an MHS e-stop only refuses further step requests. Unblocking needs an acknowledged pause whose effect the clone shows, or an SDK profile; webots_ros is not in the clone.
